questions.text: How does ColPali-style late interaction score a query against a page?

options.A: It averages every query-to-patch similarity into a single mean.
options.B: It selects one page patch and ignores all remaining query tokens.
options.C: It sums each query token’s highest similarity to any page patch.
options.D: It counts the number of characters shared by query and document IDs.

questions.explanation: MaxSim takes the maximum similarity over page patches separately for each query token, then sums those maxima.

questions.text: You replace one embedding per page with 729 patch embeddings per page, keeping dimension and numeric precision fixed. What happens to raw vector storage?

options.A: It remains unchanged because the page count is the same.
options.B: It increases by a factor of729, before compression and metadata.
options.C: It decreases because each query uses only the best-matching patch.
options.D: It becomes independent of page count because vectors are cached.

questions.explanation: Raw vector bytes scale with pages×vectors per page×dimensions×bytes per value. Replacing one vector with729 multiplies the vector storage by729.

questions.text: MaxSim receives a precomputed similarity matrix with query-token rows [[0.9, 0.2], [0.8, 0.1]]. What score does summing the row maxima produce?
questions.explanation: The maxima are0.9 and0.8, giving1.7. The same page patch may be selected by more than one query token; no one-to-one assignment is enforced.
